Title: GET productsList returns all products
Steps: 1. Send GET /api/productsList.
Expected Result: responseCode 200; every product has id, name, price "Rs. n", brand and category.

Title: product ids are unique
Steps: 1. Send GET /api/productsList and collect all product ids.
Expected Result: All product ids are unique.

Title: POST to productsList is not supported
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/productsList.
Expected Result: responseCode 405, message "This request method is not supported."

Title: GET brandsList returns all brands
Steps: 1. Send GET /api/brandsList.
Expected Result: responseCode 200 and a list of brands that includes Polo and H&M.

Title: PUT to brandsList is not supported
Steps: 1. Send PUT /api/brandsList.
Expected Result: responseCode 405.

Title: POST searchProduct returns matching products
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/searchProduct with search_product=top.
Expected Result: responseCode 200; every product matches "top" by name or category and "Blue Top" is included.

Title: searchProduct with no match returns an empty list
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/searchProduct with a term that matches nothing.
Expected Result: responseCode 200 and an empty products list.

Title: searchProduct without search_product parameter is a bad request
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/searchProduct without the search_product parameter.
Expected Result: responseCode 400, message "Bad request, search_product parameter is missing in POST request."

Title: search results are a subset of productsList
Steps: 1. Get all products, search "dress", compare the ids.
Expected Result: All search results are a subset of productsList.

Title: verifyLogin with valid credentials
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/verifyLogin with the user e-mail and password.
Expected Result: responseCode 200, message "User exists!"

Title: verifyLogin without email is a bad request
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/verifyLogin with only a password.
Expected Result: responseCode 400, message "Bad request, email or password parameter is missing in POST request."

Title: DELETE to verifyLogin is not supported
Steps: 1. Send DELETE /api/verifyLogin.
Expected Result: responseCode 405, message "This request method is not supported."

Title: verifyLogin with invalid credentials
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/verifyLogin with the correct e-mail and a wrong password.
Expected Result: responseCode 404, message "User not found!"

Title: createAccount registers a user
Steps:
1. Send POST /api/createAccount with a full unique user.
2. Send POST /api/verifyLogin with the same credentials.
Expected Result: responseCode 201 "User created!"; the login verification returns 200.

Title: createAccount with an existing e-mail is rejected
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/createAccount with the e-mail of the existing user.
Expected Result: responseCode 400, message "Email already exists!"

Title: createAccount with missing fields is a bad request
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/createAccount with only the name.
Expected Result: responseCode 400 (bad request).

Title: deleteAccount removes the user
Preconditions: A user created through the API.
Steps:
1. Send DELETE /api/deleteAccount with e-mail and password.
2. Send POST /api/verifyLogin with the same credentials.
Expected Result: responseCode 200 "Account deleted!"; the following login returns 404.

Title: deleteAccount with wrong password keeps the account
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps:
1. Send DELETE /api/deleteAccount with a wrong password.
2. Verify the user can still log in.
Expected Result: responseCode 404 and the account is kept.

Title: updateAccount changes the stored details
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps:
1. Send PUT /api/updateAccount with a new city and company.
2. Send GET /api/getUserDetailByEmail.
Expected Result: responseCode 200 "User updated!"; the profile shows the new values.

Title: getUserDetailByEmail returns the profile
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps: 1. Send GET /api/getUserDetailByEmail?email=<user e-mail>.
Expected Result: responseCode 200 and the profile (name, e-mail, first/last name, country) matches the registration.

Title: getUserDetailByEmail for an unknown e-mail
Steps: 1. Send GET /api/getUserDetailByEmail with an unregistered e-mail.
Expected Result: responseCode 404, message "Account not found with this email, try another email!"

Title: getUserDetailByEmail must not return a profile without credentials
Preconditions: A registered user exists (created through the API with a unique e-mail).
Steps: 1. Send GET /api/getUserDetailByEmail for the user WITHOUT any authentication.
Expected Result: CORRECT behaviour: no profile data for anonymous callers. Actual: full profile (PII) is returned (known defect DEF-01, marked test.fail).

Title: unsupported method should answer with HTTP 405
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/productsList (unsupported method) and read the HTTP status line and body.
Expected Result: CORRECT behaviour: HTTP 405 as well as responseCode 405. Actual: HTTP 200 (known defect DEF-04, marked test.fail).
